Enjoy figuring out how the data fits together? 
 An unfamiliar database, a tricky conversion, a migration ready to run. If that sounds like your kind of work, we’d like to hear from you!
 We’re looking for an Intermediate ETL Developer to join Pandell-ESG's Project Services team. You’ll help customers move their data into our software and work alongside a strong team that’s ready to roll up their sleeves and help.
 About the role 
 You’ll work through the details of each migration: understanding the customer’s data, planning how it needs to be converted, and writing the scripts to make it happen. You’ll learn different data models, adapt our conversion tools, and troubleshoot along the way.
 You’ll also have opportunities to take the technical lead on small to medium-sized projects and help other team members build their skills and confidence. It’s a role for someone who enjoys hands-on technical work and wants to take on more responsibility with a team behind them.
 Your team 
 Our Project Services team helps customers implement software across Pandell’s suite of more than 12 product groups. You’ll work with colleagues who understand the software and the business processes behind it, sharing ideas, and working through challenges together.
 About Us: 
 ESG, along with its subsidiary Pandell, is a global leader in energy software, providing Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solutions that support companies across utilities, renewables, retail energy, and oil and gas.
 Across North America and the UK, our combined platforms help teams manage key parts of their business, including billing, asset management, regulatory requirements, and geospatial data. These tools bring together the information and workflows teams rely on every day, making it easier to run operations and stay organized.
 Through cloud-based technology and data-driven insights, we help energy companies navigate complex markets and continue progressing toward Net-Zero goals.
 Life at Pandell-ESG 
 We care about doing good work and being good people to work with. That means making room for questions, listening to different perspectives, and helping each other when the work gets complicated.
 We want people to feel welcome, respected, and comfortable being themselves. You’ll have the trust, tools, and flexibility to do your work, along with support from your teammates.
 What you'll do: 
 Plan data migrations, turning project requirements into a technical approach.
 Write and run conversion scripts to move data between systems.
 Develop tools and make changes to our conversion frameworks to meet project needs.
 Get to know customers’ data and business processes, working through unfamiliar data models with support from senior teammates.
 Take the technical lead on small to medium-sized projects, helping plan the work, estimate effort, and keep technical tasks on track.
 Review code and test other developers’ work, with guidance when needed, to check that it meets project requirements and team standards.
 Troubleshoot issues during development, configuration, and performance tuning.
 Keep technical documentation clear and accurate, and talk through technical questions with colleagues.
 Help other developers build their skills and confidence through mentoring and feedback.
 What you’ll bring 
 5+ years of hands-on experience working with SQL, SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS), and Oracle databases.
 Experience writing complex queries and data conversion scripts, with a solid understanding of database tables and how they relate to one another.
 Knowledge of T-SQL, PL/SQL, C#, and PowerShell for ETL scripting and tool development.
 Experience with ETL processes, data migrations, and conversion frameworks, including writing and running scripts of moderate complexity.
 Experience building tools and making changes to existing frameworks.
 An understanding of relational and non-relational databases.
 Familiarity with the software development life cycle and how it applies to data conversion, configuration, and deployment.
 The ability to guide technical work on a project and review code against requirements and quality standards.
 Good judgement when planning your work, estimating how long tasks will take, and managing competing deadlines.
 Clear communication, attention to detail, and the ability to work both independently and as part of a team.
 Curiosity about unfamiliar systems and an interest in continuing to learn.
 Post-secondary education in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related technical field.
 Bonus points for: 
 Experience with Visual Studio, Microsoft Access, Excel, GitHub, Jira, or TeamCity.
 Knowledge of the energy industry, particularly land administration or land management.
 We’d love to see your work. If you have a GitHub profile or code samples you’re able to share, include a link with your application.
 What’s In It for You? 
 At Pandell-ESG, we believe in  creating a workplace where you can do your best work  while enjoying  meaningful projects and a strong sense of belonging . 
 Here are just a few things we offer:
 Work-from-home or office flexibility - choose where you work best!
 Flexible hours to support work-life balance 
 Competitive benefits package, including 100% dental reimbursement 
 Retirement Savings Plan with company matching 
 Training budget and professional development opportunities 
 Fully stocked kitchen at the office with healthy options, snacks, and plenty of coffee 
 A fun and engaging culture with virtual and in-person events, learning opportunities, and a games room and lounge 
 A wellness budget to support your version of wellbeing
 Join us and be part of something EPIC. 
 If you’re excited about helping customers succeed, bringing software to life through training , and collaborating with an incredible team , we’d love to hear from you!

The Body Shop Parts Handler is responsible for the physical receipt, verification, organization, and internal distribution of automotive parts within the collision center. This role focuses entirely on ensuring that the correct parts flow efficiently from the delivery to the technicians' bays.
 Responsibilities
 1. Receiving & Mirror-Matching:
 Inspect all incoming parts shipments for physical damage, defects upon delivery.
 Perform strict "mirror-matching" by physically comparing new replacement parts against the damaged original parts on the vehicle to ensure 100% accuracy before production begins.
 Verify delivered items against invoices and repair orders (ROs).
 2. Inventory Control & Logistics:
 Unbox, label, and securely store all incoming parts in designated job bins or staging areas.
 Maintain a clean, organized, and safe parts department, tracking the location of all components.
 Track and manage supplemental parts deliveries for ongoing repair jobs.
 3. Internal Distribution:
 Proactively deliver correct components to assigned auto body technicians, painters, and assemblers at their work bays.
 Communicate parts status updates immediately to technicians and production managers to prevent workflow delays.
 4. Administrative & Returns Tracking:
 Process packing slips, update inventory logs, and enter parts receiving data into the shop’s management software.
 Identify, document, and process incorrect or damaged parts for immediate return to vendors.
 Track core charges and ensure old cores are organized and ready for vendor pickup.
 Experience:
 Previous experience in an automotive collision center preferred.
 Technical Skills:
 Basic computer proficiency; experience with shop management systems (e.g., BodyShop Connect, Mitchell, Audatex, Microsoft Outlook) is an asset.
 Physical Requirements:
 Ability to lift up to 50 lbs independently, stand for extended periods, and safely navigate a busy workshop environment.
 Attention to Detail:
 Exceptional precision required for identifying subtle differences in automotive trim, body lines, and model variations during mirror-matching.

 Help evolve DV infrastructure including regression flows, CI/CD integration, EDA compute environments, and reproducible setups.

 Consumer Banking: Consumer Banking builds financial products for the millions of employees paid through Gusto, anchored to Gusto Wallet — spend accounts, savings goals, paycheck splitting, and on-demand access to earned wages.  Gusto Money: MoneyOS is the team within Gusto Money focused on helping small businesses better understand, manage, and improve their financial position.  HR Experiences (HRX): HRX helps small businesses get expert HR help right inside the product — a customer simply says what they need, and Gusto takes the action, answers the question, or brings in a human expert when the stakes are high.  Own design end to end in your domain — from framing ambiguous problems to shipping high-craft, accessible experiences that hide the underlying complexity from customers.
 Shape goals, priorities, and roadmap in partnership with your PM and engineering lead, balancing customer trust, business value, and technical realities.
 Translate ambiguous, often 0→1 strategy into clear scopes, flows, and interaction patterns — including patterns that don't yet exist at Gusto.
 Design the experience of AI thoughtfully — representing uncertainty, surfacing errors gracefully, preserving customer agency, and knowing when a human should step in.
 Ground your decisions in customer insight, leading or partnering on research, competitive audits, and hypothesis-driven exploration in high-stakes, sometimes compliance-sensitive domains.
 Raise the craft and systems bar, evolving Gusto's design system where existing patterns fall short.
 Work in fast cycles and use AI tools in your own practice — set a clear target, prototype and ship real things to customers, and let what you learn sharpen the direction.

 6+ years of product design experience owning and shipping end-to-end work, ideally in B2B SaaS, fintech, or another high-trust domain, with strong craft across web.
 Experience designing AI-enabled or conversational experiences shipped to real users, and you can speak concretely to how you handled uncertainty, errors, and human override.
 Comfort with ambiguity and 0→1, you frame the problem, scope the work, and move forward without waiting for perfect information.

 Judgment to evaluate and direct AI outputs, when to use them, when to override them, and how to raise the bar, especially where the cost of being wrong is high.

 Background contributing to AI governance, evaluation practices, or AI experience design patterns.

 Être à l’emploi d’Abbott 
 En étant à l’emploi d’Abbott, vous pourrez faire un travail qui compte, vous perfectionner et apprendre, prendre soin de vous et des membres de votre famille, rester fidèle à ce que vous êtes et vivre pleinement. Vous pourrez :

 L’occasion à saisir 
 Ce poste est basé à notre bureau à St-Laurent, au sein de la division Nutrition et nécessite une présence au bureau quatre jours par semaine, avec la possibilité de travailler à distance une journée.
 Le chef principal, Publicité numérique chez les détaillants, va diriger l’élaboration et la mise en œuvre de la stratégie auprès de nos principaux partenaires de vente au détail, comme Amazon Canada, Walmart Canada et Loblaw (PC Optimum/Advance).

 Ce que vous ferez 
 Portée et retombées 
 • Gérer et optimiser un budget annuel de plusieurs millions de dollars destiné à la publicité sur les plateformes des détaillants et au commerce numérique sur diverses plateformes importantes
 • Influencer la planification commerciale conjointe et les stratégies de croissance de catégorie auprès des grands détaillants canadiens

 Équipe et méthode de travail

 • Diriger et gérer le réseau d’agences externes, en étant responsable des relations avec les partenaires, en donnant des directives et en assurant une bonne exécution, tout en conservant un grand contrôle sur la stratégie à l’interne
 • Superviser toutes les étapes des projets de publicité chez les détaillants et de commerce numérique, en veillant au respect des délais et des normes de qualité, et à l’atteinte des objectifs
 • Servir d’intermédiaire principal entre les services concernés, en reliant les stratégies en matière de commerce, de médias et de clients pour favoriser une croissance cohérente et réplicable
 Principales responsabilités 
 • Être responsable de la stratégie commerciale et de la publicité sur les plateformes des détaillants
 • Diriger la stratégie de publicité sur les plateformes des détaillants et son exécution auprès d’Amazon Ads, de Walmart Connect et de Loblaw Advance
 • Assurer la performance du commerce numérique chez les principaux détaillants, afin de stimuler la croissance et la rentabilité.

 • Gérer les agences externes tout en veillant à ce que l’orientation stratégique demeure à l’interne

 • Établir de relations solides avec les détaillants afin de positionner Abbott comme chef de file de la croissance de catégorie

 • Contribuer à la planification commerciale conjointe avec les grands détaillants, en profitant de leur potentiel de croissance
 Présence des produits en ligne 
 • Optimiser la présence des produits en ligne chez tous les détaillants : qualité des fiches produits, exactitude du contenu et conformité; référencement sur les plateformes des détaillants; notes, avis et leviers de conversion

 Analyses et mesures

 Intégration à la gestion de la relation client

 Primary Purpose 
 The Academic Services Coordinator provides a broad spectrum of responsibilities including but not limited to client service, academic integrity, scheduling, support for core functions (e.g. recruitment and admissions, internal and external events etc.), special projects, data management, and general administrative duties. The position acts as a liaison with units in the Faculty of Engineering and central university services as it relates to key accountabilities. Reporting to the Manager, Academic Services and Engagement or Manager, Graduate Studies (Manager), the Academic Services Coordinator provides exceptional client support for academic programs within the Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering.

 Key Accountabilities 
 Client Service

 Student Experience Administration – Provides a welcoming experience by delivering exceptional service in a student-centered environment.  Program Administration - Provides administrative support to the Associate Chairs and Chair in all matters relating to the undergraduate and graduate programs. Deliver immediate support to students in distress; follow up with appropriate referrals. Coach students on personal matters as appropriate especially addressing inclusion of diversity, access and accommodations for disabilities. Maintain current knowledge related to student wellness and disseminate information and knowledge to faculty and other department staff.
 Academic Integrity Management – Promotes and facilitates an environment that focuses on academic integrity. The incumbent advises students and faculty on academic integrity matters and academic misconduct. The incumbent acts as an expert resource and provides information on relevant policies and process. The Academic Services Coordinator works with the Associate Chairs and Manager on academic offence cases within the Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering ensuring files are appropriately and accurately managed to completion. 
 Communications – Works in conjunction with multiple stakeholders within the Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering, Faculty of Engineering and central units to develop communications as it relates to recruitment, admissions, scheduling, academic integrity, policy and best practice. The incumbent is responsible for developing and delivering consistent, professional, and creative internal communications to engage students. 
 Support for Special Projects – The Academic Services Coordinator provides expert support on 
 special projects and strategic initiatives as directed by the Administrative Officer, Manager, Associate Chairs, and the Chair. The incumbent participates in and contributes to discussions on special projects consistent with the Department’s strategic priorities, including enhancing student experience. The Academic Services Coordinator may be required to consult with key stakeholders to understand diverse needs.
 Support for Core Functions – The Academic Services Coordinator operates as part of a larger team contributing to various core functions in the Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering. Duties may include administrative support and event planning, supporting the recruitment and admissions process, etc. The incumbent may be required to support advising, scheduling, etc. as needed to ensure efficiency in operations.
 Data Collection and Management – The Academic Services Coordinator supports senior leadership on a variety of data needs including but not limited to data collection, management, warehousing. Provides support to various committees on matters relating to program accreditation.
 General Administrative Support 
 Serves as a resource for the application of policies, procedures, guidelines, and best practices.
 Supports the activities of the Associate Chairs, Manager, and Administrative Officer
 Contributes to the enhancement of student-centered service models.
 Contributes to the development of various reports, presentations, communications, etc.
 Supports time sensitive key accountabilities of other administrative roles as required. The Academic Services Coordinator demonstrates breadth and depth of knowledge in all aspects of the role.·

 University degree; equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered.
 Familiarity with engineering discipline and relevant academic policies is an asset.
 Experience

 Experience pertaining to undergraduate and graduate programs is an asset.
 Ability to work collaboratively with all team members to deliver excellent results with accuracy and integrity in a student-centered environment.
 Knowledge/Skills/Abilities

You turn scrollers into followers… and followers into customers. You know how to make people stop, watch, follow, click… and buy. Likes are nice. Views are nice. But sales are nicer. Because great organic social doesn’t just build an audience. It earns attention, builds trust, and turns that trust into measurable revenue.
 If that sounds like you, you might have what it takes to become our next Organic Social Specialist. 
 Small Print ⇒ We’re not looking for a “like junkie.” We want someone who knows how to grow a social audience and turn that attention into sales. Someone who understands that followers, views, and engagement are only useful if they build trust, drive traffic, and ultimately help customers buy. If you measure success by views alone then this probably isn’t the role for you.
 Still here?
 Okay then…
 This job will give you ALL the feels: 
 We create clinically supported, natural solutions for some of the biggest health challenges women over 40 face today. And your work will help more women discover those solutions. You’ll help us become a brand these women actually want to follow. You’ll help create the posts that make her stop. The videos she sends to a friend. The content that makes her think, “Finally. Someone actually gets it.”
 If that excites you, you’ll find no better place to continue your career than here.
 This job might be for you if… 
 You understand what makes people stop scrolling . Hooks. Thumbnails. First frames. Captions. Curiosity. Emotion. Pattern interrupts. Trends. You don’t need someone to explain why the first two seconds of a TikTok matter. You already spend more time than is probably healthy wondering why one piece of content gets 327 views while another gets 327,000.
 You know every platform speaks a slightly different language. TikTok isn’t Instagram. Instagram isn’t Facebook. YouTube isn’t Reddit. And taking the exact same post, resizing it four times, and calling it a “social strategy” makes a small part of you die inside. You know how to adapt an idea to the platform, audience, format, and reason somebody is there in the first place.
 You can actually create the stuff. We’re not looking for someone who just sits in meetings talking about content pillars. You’ll help develop ideas, write briefs, schedule content, coordinate assets, get everything live, and make sure the little details don’t fall through the cracks.
 You’ve got a nose for a good trend. Sounds. Formats. Memes. Conversations. Creators. Questions people suddenly can’t stop asking. You pay attention to what’s happening online and can tell the difference between a trend we should jump on… and one that will make a women’s health company look like someone’s dad discovered TikTok.
 You’re obsessed with the audience. What are women talking about? What are they frustrated by? What are they asking in the comments? What myths keep popping up? What are competitors saying? What language are real women actually using? You know some of the best content ideas won’t come from a brainstorm. They’ll come from listening.
 You care about results more than vanity metrics. Followers and likes are lovely. But you also want to know what people clicked, what sent traffic to the site, what converted, what content assisted a sale, and what we should do differently next month. Because ultimately, we’re not trying to win a trophy for “nicest Instagram grid.”
 Numbers don’t make your eyes glaze over. Reach. Engagement. Clicks. Conversion. Follower growth. Traffic. UTMs. GA4. You don’t have to be a data scientist wearing six monitors and muttering about statistical significance. But you should be able to look at performance, spot patterns, and turn what you learn into better content.
 You know how to use social scheduling tools without needing an emergency tutorial. Hootsuite, Sprout Social, Later, Buffer, or something similar. We don’t care which logo you’ve stared at most. We care that you understand how to plan, schedule, organize, and manage a social calendar without everything descending into chaos.
 You can turn performance into strategy. You don’t just send a monthly report containing 17 charts and the groundbreaking observation that “engagement was up.” You ask why. What worked? What flopped? Which topics got attention? Which formats drove clicks? What should we do more of? Less of? Test next? The report is only useful if it changes what we do.
 You’re organised enough to keep a lot of little moving pieces moving. Content calendars. Briefs. Designers. Video. Approvals. Links. UTMs. Scheduling. Launch dates. Reporting. Somebody has to keep track of it all. Preferably without sending 14 Slack messages asking, “Any update on this?”
 You play nicely with others. You’ll work with Content, Creative, Acquisition, Email, Influencer, Customer Service and other teams across the business. Sometimes you’ll need something from them. Sometimes they’ll need something from you. You communicate clearly, follow up, solve problems, and understand that being easy to work with is a genuine career superpower.
 You know social never stops changing . Algorithm updates. New features. New formats. Social commerce. Search behaviour. Yesterday’s “best practice” suddenly dying a very public death. You’re curious enough to keep learning without somebody having to chase you around the office waving an industry newsletter.
 You’ve got at least a year of experience in social media marketing or something closely related. Maybe you’ve managed brand accounts. Maybe you’ve built social for an ecommerce company. Maybe you’ve helped grow a community, supported creator campaigns, or owned organic content as part of a broader marketing role. What matters most is that you can show us you’ve done the work and learned from it.
 Women’s health genuinely interests you. You don’t need to arrive knowing everything about women’s health. But you do need to care enough to learn. We’re talking about real health concerns affecting millions of women, so curiosity, empathy, accuracy, and good judgment matter.
 Bonus points if you’ve worked with Shopify, ecommerce brands, Google Sheets, Jira, Confluence, or similar tools.
 Double bonus points if you already have strong opinions about why most brand TikToks are painfully boring.
 Now, time to be honest… is this really you?
 If you’ve already started thinking about what you’d post first, which competitors you’d stalk, and how you’d build our first 10,000 followers…
 We should probably talk. 
 We don’t expect you to know everything. This isn’t a “12 years of TikTok experience required” job ad. But we do want somebody curious, switched on, commercially minded, organised, and hungry to get very, very good at organic social.
 And someone who sees a brand starting from scratch and thinks:
 Ohhh… this could be fun. 
 Other Qualities You’ll Need
 We’re going to insist that you have these 3 qualities:
 You’re humble — you put the team and others’ needs ahead of your own.
 You’re hungry — you want to learn more, improve, and keep getting better.
 You’re people-smart — in the sense that you’re a great teammate.
 The truth is, if you don’t have these qualities, you won’t last long at our company.
 So if you’re missing one of them, be honest. Save yourself a lot of headaches and skip to a job posting that’s a better fit for you.
 What Will You Earn?
 We believe in rewarding top talent.
 So let’s talk about salary once we’ve had the chance to get to know you better. Rest assured, we’re generous and offer above-market pay for the right person. If you bring the skills, curiosity, and hunger to grow, we’ll make sure the compensation reflects that.
 You’ll also enjoy the following benefits:
 A generous healthcare package
 Monthly team events and activities
 Flexible Stat Holidays with the option to bank days for later use
 Weekly team lunches
 Casual dress code
 An incredible dog-friendly office
 And above all, you’ll join a team that you’ll never want to leave.
 Culture is everything to us.
 Yes, we work extremely hard to change as many people’s lives as possible.
 But we know how to have fun and reward ourselves too.
 How To Apply
 So, do you have what it takes to become the next member of Team AlgaeCal?
 Job opportunities like this don’t come along often, and we’ve got a lot to offer the right person.
 So, to make sure our future Organic Social Specialist is the real deal, will be a great fit, and will thrive here, we ask a little more than your run-of-the-mill job application.

 Why are you the best Organic Social Specialist for this role? Give us examples of accounts, campaigns, or content you’ve worked on — and include results where possible.
 Describe why you fit perfectly with our values. Read them here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1deCCJZ6tiDiOSlr_W0UdCuM_V_ahzPBs/view 
 What’s the toughest challenge you’ve ever overcome in your life? How did you overcome it?

 And tell us what you actually did. 
 If something performed particularly well, even better. Give us the numbers.

Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked. 
 That is the whole job.
 Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.
 So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.
 At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.
 You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.
 Here is what "end to end" actually means.
 You are the account manager. We do not have any.  You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
 You own the whole funnel, not the campaign.  Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
 You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it.  We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.
 You can live anywhere.  We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.
 If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.
 If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
 What the job looks like 
 Own a set of DTC accounts  as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
 Own the client relationship.  There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
 Audit before you touch anything.  Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
 Run brand and non brand as different businesses.  Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
 Know what PMax is actually doing.  The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
 Keep Google's automation on a leash.  Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
 Own the feed.  Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
 Own the tracking.  GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
 Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it.  Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
 Build the things the account needs.  Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.
 You are a fit if 
 You have done this with real money.  Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
 You are fluent in the whole stack , not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
 You are AI native, and you build.  This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
 You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level.  You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
 You are skeptical of your own numbers.  You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
 You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls.  Where you live is up to you.
 Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.
 You are not a fit if 
 "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
 You want to be told what to do this week.
 You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
 You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.
 Why this role is exciting 
 This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.
 You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.
 You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.
 You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

 In this role, you'll help our product designers move from intent to launch in more fluid, faster ways, while making sure everything we ship draws on the high-quality, evolving design language of our product. At times, you'll take point on larger cross-functional efforts, from new agent workflows to design-to-code. Our AI practice in design is still taking shape, and you'll be one of the people defining it.

 Take point on building agents and skills that use the system to turn a request like "a renewal modal offering 14 days free" into on-brand, legally approved, production-ready design
 Translate design judgment into evals and review agents that check work before it ships, such as an agent that reviews designs against approved legal and content patterns, and use what they catch to improve the system

 Get energy from making other designers faster and better, and measure your impact by what the team ships

 Care as much about choosing the right default as designing the full range of possibilities

About the Role
 You will be the person who makes our AI better at selling. You will read its conversations, notice what is working and what is not, and change the instructions it follows so the next thousand conversations go better.
 You do not need to know everything on day one. We will teach you our tools, our playbooks and how to write and test prompts. What we cannot teach is the instinct for conversations, a feel for sales, and the curiosity to dig into the data and ask why.
 What You'll Do
 Review AI-drafted text messages each day, and approve, edit or rewrite them before they send.
 Spot patterns across conversations, such as an opener that gets replies but no orders, and figure out the cause.
 Update each brand's prompts and playbook to fix problems at the source, then test the change before it goes live.
 Respond to brand requests and turn them into playbook updates.
 Help launch new brands: deep research on their brand, write the persona and opening messages, and check that offers work.
 Run and track A/B tests, and report what won. 
 You read people well. From one text you can tell whether a shopper is ready to buy, has a question, or is done, and you reply the way a real person would.
 You have sales instinct. You answer an objection and then ask for the sale, without arguing or pushing the customer away.
 You are curious about data. You can open a table of conversations and ask the right questions: how many, compared to what, at which brand, since when. You notice when a number looks off and go find out why.
 You fix the cause, not the symptom. When the AI says something wrong, you look for the reason (a missing fact, a vague rule, two rules that conflict) and fix the instruction so it does not happen again.
 You are comfortable with AI tools. You use ChatGPT, Claude or similar tools regularly and understand that how you ask shapes what you get back.
 You are online. These are live conversations. You are responsive during working hours and quick to pick things up in Slack.
 You learn fast and like feedback. You pick up new tools quickly and want to get better each week.
 Nice to Have
 Experience in sales (SDR, BDR, retail or any role with a close rate), customer support, or live chat.
 Experience at a DTC brand or ecommerce agency.
 Familiarity with Shopify, Klaviyo, Postscript or similar tools.
 Spreadsheet skills, or basic SQL.
 Something you have built or automated with AI on your own.
 What We'll Teach You
 Our console, approval queue and playbook system.
 How to write, test and ship prompt changes.
 Shopify basics, discount codes and how they combine.
 How we run and read A/B tests.

About Foresight  
 Foresight's mission is to bring the world's critical infrastructure into service faster by better enabling teams to deliver complex capital projects. 
 The AI buildout runs on physical things: data centers, power, and the supply chains behind them. A single hyperscale campus involves an owner, a general contractor, dozens of trades, long-lead equipment suppliers, lenders and commissioning teams. Each works from its own schedule and its own spreadsheets. When a project slips, the people who could fix it usually find out last. For an AI data center, a month late can mean tens of millions in lost revenue. 
 Foresight is the control tower for these projects. We connect schedules, field progress and execution data across every party, forecast where delivery is heading, and help teams act before a delay becomes a missed date. On one 15-project portfolio, Foresight found a project 245 days behind, cut reporting overhead by 90%, and helped prevent more than $100M in lost revenue. 
 We work with top data-center owners, developers and general contractors across the world, including Crusoe, Applied Digital, and NTT. We raised a $25M Series A led by Macquarie Capital and are headquartered in New York. 
 The role  
 We're looking for a Senior Platform Engineer to build the cloud foundation that Foresight runs on. 
 You will design and run the infrastructure, delivery pipelines and observability that let every engineer ship safely and often. You will make the platform secure and compliant by default, so enterprise customers can trust it with their most important project data. This is a hands-on role on a new team, for someone who treats the platform as a product and measures success by how fast and safely others can ship on it. 
 At Foresight, the platform is a product, and our engineers are its customers. You make the right way to build, ship and run software also the easiest way. This could translate to work on: 
 Cloud foundation: Design our AWS environments as code, from networking and compute to managed databases and storage, so any environment can be rebuilt from scratch with confidence. 
 Delivery pipelines: Build CI/CD that takes a merged change to production safely, with automated tests, security scanning, preview environments and fast rollback. 
 Observability on a budget: Build logging, metrics, tracing and alerting that show what every service is doing, without letting monitoring costs run away. 
 Security and compliance by default: Build identity and access controls, secrets management, encryption and audit trails that meet enterprise standards such as SOC 2 and ISO 27001. 
 Reliability at scale: Build autoscaling, backups, disaster recovery and incident response, and deploy in the regions our customers' data must stay in. 
 What you'll do  
 Treat other engineers as your customers: build paved roads, templates and self-service tools they actually want to use. 
 Keep the platform as simple as the problem allows. 
 Automate everything that reaches production; no manual changes to live systems. 
 Own cloud cost: make spend visible by service and customer, and keep it in line as we grow. 
 Lead incident response and blameless postmortems, then fix the root cause so it doesn't happen twice. 
 Help set the team's infrastructure standards and shape the platform as one of its first platform engineers. 
 You might be a fit if you  
 Have 5+ years of experience building and running production infrastructure on AWS, with ownership of uptime and cost. 
 Are strong in infrastructure-as-code skills with Terraform, CDK or similar, including modules others reuse. 
 Have experience running containerized services on AWS, such as ECS, EKS or Lambda, and knowing when each fits. 
 Have built and owned CI/CD pipelines, including automated testing, deployment strategies and rollback. 
 Are hands-on with observability: logs, metrics, traces, SLOs and alerting that people trust. 
 Have solid grounding in cloud security: IAM least privilege, network design, secrets management and encryption. 
 Are comfortable writing code in Python, Go or a similar language to build tooling and automation. 
 Are calm and clear in communication during incidents and comfortable making pragmatic trade-offs on a small team. 
 Bonus points  
 Hands-on with OpenTelemetry and open observability tools such as Grafana, Prometheus or Loki. 
 Prepared a company for SOC 2, ISO 27001 or similar audits, including automated evidence collection. 
 Experience with GitOps, progressive delivery (canary or blue-green) and supply-chain security (image signing, SBOMs). 
 Operated multi-region or data-residency deployments, including in regulated or public-sector environments. 
 Experience running infrastructure for ML and AI workloads, including GPU or hosted model services. 
 FinOps experience: cost allocation, rightsizing and savings plans. 
 Early-stage or founding-team experience. 
 None of these are required. If the core of this role excites you, apply. 
 Why join now  
 Real stakes, real customers . Real stakes, real customers. You won't be building for a hypothetical buyer. Owners and contractors are building now, on deadlines measured in revenue per day. 
 Blank canvas, solid ground . You get first-engineer level scope on a product that already has paying customers, real data and proven outcomes to tell. 
 Defining a category .Agentic software for physical infrastructure is a new category. What you build will become the standard. 
 Small, senior team . Flat, direct, low on process. We debate openly, decide quickly and ship.  
 Compensation and location  
 Total Comp : $180,000-240,000, based on experience, level, and location.
 Benefits : Health, Dental, Vision, 401(k), PTO . 
 Location : New York, San Francisco, and Montreal are preferred. Occasional travel to may be required.
 Foresight is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of every background and do not discriminate on any protected basis.

En tant qu’organisation RDQA indépendante, notre engagement consiste à faire de l’excellence qualité un avantage stratégique à toutes les étapes de la découverte et du développement, tout au long du cycle de vie du produit, afin de permettre sa concrétisation et d’accélérer l’accès de nos patients à des traitements innovants.
 L’empreinte mondiale des essais cliniques de R&D d’AbbVie s’est élargie en raison de la croissance du portefeuille et de la complexité du développement mondial, entraînant une augmentation globale du nombre d’essais internationaux menés dans les filiales. En outre, l’acquisition d’Allergan et son intégration à AbbVie ont considérablement augmenté le nombre d’essais cliniques gérés par les filiales. RDQA AREA met l’accent sur la gestion proactive de la qualité et sur les résultats qualité afin de soutenir le développement clinique et l’organisation R&D dans les pays désignés à travers le monde.
 AREA soutient les pays d’Europe, des Amériques et de la région Intercontinentale, tels que définis par AbbVie. Les résultats attendus dans les filiales comprennent l’excellence qualité, la réalisation des buts et objectifs de R&D en vue de la soumission de nouvelles thérapies, notamment le respect du One AbbVie Quality System’, la mise en œuvre du ‘RDQA Quality System Excellence’ (CAPA, gestion du changement, gestion des risques qualité et normes documentaires), ainsi que la garantie de l’intégrité des données.
 Le périmètre comprend les activités de R&D et de recherche clinique menées par les filiales ou par AbbVie dans la région, dans le but d’obtenir les approbations dès la première soumission et ainsi de faire progresser le portefeuille.
 Ce poste relève de l’Associate Director RDQA ou du Global Director RDQA, AREA.
 Principales responsabilités 
 Le/la Senior Manager RDQA AREA apportera son soutien aux pays et à la région qui lui sont attribués et sera responsable de la mise en œuvre et de l’exécution des activités liées à la gestion proactive de la qualité clinique. Les principales responsabilités sont les suivantes :
 Maintenir une relation étroite et collaborative avec les fonctions RDQA ayant une incidence sur la recherche clinique au sein des filiales désignées dans les pays et la région attribués.
 Établir des relations de travail collaboratives avec les responsables et les équipes du développement clinique au sein des filiales désignées afin de faire progresser le ‘AbbVie Quality System’, de promouvoir l’excellence qualité et d’obtenir l’autorisation de mise sur le marché dès la première soumission auprès des autorités de santé.
 Superviser la qualité et la conformité dans un environnement réglementé, notamment au regard des politiques et procédures d’AbbVie ainsi que des normes et réglementations nationales et régionales.
 Diriger et/ou soutenir l’élaboration de stratégies d’identification, d’atténuation ou de maîtrise des risques pour les activités de recherche clinique, y compris les essais cliniques menés dans les pays désignés, avec des revues périodiques des données de qualité et de conformité dans une optique d’amélioration continue.

ABOUT FUSE

We are building one of the most potentially consequential companies of the century. Our mission is to accelerate the world's transition to fusion energy while safeguarding humankind. This is not a normal company. This is not a normal job. We are committed for the long term to win.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As an Electrical Engineer at Fuse, you're building at the limit of what's possible, advancing pulsed-power technology as part of a team tackling the monumental challenge of fusion energy.




CORE RESPONSIBILITIES

Design, build, and test control and data acquisition (DAQ) systems for pulsed-power facilities.

Design and assemble PCBs for control systems, diagnostics, and pulsed-power applications.

Diagnose, troubleshoot, and analyze the performance of electrical components, assemblies, and systems.

Develop control architectures spanning sensing, actuation, embedded hardware, and data acquisition.

Conduct applied R&D across electrical engineering, fusion energy, and pulsed-power systems.

Write specifications and technical reports and support systems through build, testing, and iteration.




MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering or equivalent experience.

1+ years of experience in PCB schematic and layout design using Altium Designer or equivalent software.

1+ years of experience simulating electronic circuits using SPICE.

1+ years of experience designing control processes and control systems, including defining control architecture, sensing, and actuation.

1+ years of experience configuring and managing data acquisition (DAQ) systems.

Proficiency with lab equipment, including oscilloscopes, power supplies, and DMMs, as well as sensors and calibration techniques.

Experience with embedded hardware system design.

Ability and willingness to travel between Fuse locations as needed.




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

C and/or Python programming ability.

Experience with pulsed-power, high-voltage, or high-current systems.

Familiarity with EMI hardening and protected I/O for electrically noisy environments.

Hands-on experience with embedded protocols such as SPI, I2C, UART, CAN, RS-485, or Ethernet.




WHAT WE VALUE

Give a shit. Build things you're proud of.

Take responsibility. If something is broken and you can fix it, fix it. See things through.

Move fast. Make decisions, learn quickly, and keep moving forward.

Think bigger. Simplify relentlessly. Don't default to the safe answer.

Disagree and commit. The best idea wins. Once a decision is made, we move.

Desire to win. This is hard. Expect intensity. We are here to win.

Plan B is to make Plan A work.




ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

Must be able to travel and work extended hours/weekends as needed.




BENEFITS

Medical, dental, and vision coverage.

Relocation assistance for roles that require it.

Flexible time off. Take what you need, no accrual tracking.

2 weeks of paid time off built into the end of each year, subject to team and business needs.

Supportive leave of absence policies.

Paid leave for new parents.





ITAR REQUIREMENTS

To conform to U.S. Government technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.




EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

Fuse is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with Fuse is governed on the basis of merit, competence, and qualifications and will not be influenced by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, ancestry, immigration status, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability, or any other legally protected status.

You will identify computational and communication bottlenecks, implement high-performance kernels using AscendC, Triton, and TileLang, and optimize distributed acceleration suites (MindSpeed / open-source training frameworks).

The Opportunity 
 We are seeking a highly motivated and proactive Endpoint Performance Specialist to join our Digital IT team. In this fast-paced role, you will be responsible for designing, implementing, and optimizing endpoint management, automation, and performance engineering solutions that enhance the digital employee experience across a global organization. Working closely with Infrastructure, Security, and Operations teams, you will drive initiatives focused on endpoint reliability, compliance, security, and operational efficiency through modern device management and automation.
 The Endpoint Performance Specialist provides technical expertise, strategic guidance, and operational support as a key member of the Digital IT team. In partnership with internal stakeholders, you will develop scalable automation solutions, optimize Windows endpoint performance, manage Intune and security policies, and leverage digital experience insights to deliver a seamless and productive user experience. The ideal candidate will possess strong problem-solving and analytical skills, excellent communication and collaboration abilities, and a passion for automation, continuous improvement, and delivering exceptional technology experiences.
 Essential Duties and Responsibilities 
 Endpoint Management and Automation 
 Design, develop, and maintain enterprise-scale automation solutions for endpoint provisioning, configuration, remediation, security enforcement, and lifecycle management
 Develop advanced PowerShell and Python automation frameworks to reduce manual operational effort and improve service reliability
 Build proactive remediation and self-healing solutions using Microsoft Intune, Endpoint Analytics, DEX platforms, and Windows native capabilities
 Automate endpoint health checks, compliance validation, software deployment, performance optimization, and security policy enforcement
 Integrate automation with Microsoft Graph API, Azure Automation, Power Automate, and other enterprise management platforms
 Establish automation standards, governance, code reviews, testing methodologies, and documentation best practices
 Identify opportunities to eliminate repetitive operational tasks and drive continuous improvement through automation
 Performance Engineering & Troubleshooting 
 Perform advanced diagnostics for boot/login delays, application slowness, memory/CPU bottlenecks, and storage I/O issues
 Utilize tools such as Windows Performance Analyzer (WPA), Windows Performance Recorder (WPR), Sysinternals Suite, PerfMon, ProcMon, and ETW tracing
 Define and maintain endpoint performance baselines and implement proactive monitoring strategies
 Conduct root cause analysis of recurring endpoint performance issues and recommend long-term solutions
 Endpoint Imaging & Deployment Automation 
 Design, maintain, and optimize Windows 11 golden images for large-scale enterprise deployment
 Automate OS and application deployments using Intune (Autopilot) and Azure AD
 Develop and maintain PowerShell scripts for image updates, driver integration, and application packaging
 Implement zero-touch provisioning and streamline device onboarding processes
 Intune & Security Policy Management 
 Configure and manage Intune endpoint policies, compliance rules, and Autopilot deployments
 Implement and maintain Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) policies to enforce application security and compliance without compromising performance
 Align endpoint configurations with enterprise security baselines (BitLocker, Microsoft Defender, CIS, and MDM policies)
 Collaborate with Security teams to ensure balance between performance, optimization, automation, and compliance
 Digital Employee Experience (DEX) Monitoring 
 Use DEX tools (e.g., Aternity, Nexthink, or equivalent) to monitor user experience, identify performance gaps, and improve endpoint reliability
 Analyze telemetry and feedback to drive continuous improvement in end-user productivity and satisfaction
 Integrate DEX insights with automation to create proactive remediation and self-healing solutions
 Minimum Qualifications 
 4–6 years of experience in Windows endpoint engineering, automation, imaging, and performance optimization
 Strong expertise in Windows 11 internals (boot process, registry, kernel processes, OS servicing)
 Hands-on experience with Microsoft Intune (Autopilot, Endpoint Security, Compliance, Analytics)
 Proven experience implementing and managing Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC)
 Strong automation engineering experience with PowerShell scripting, Microsoft Graph API, Intune automation, proactive remediations, and endpoint self-healing solutions
 Ability to design scalable automation frameworks and eliminate manual operational processes
 Proficiency in automation and scripting (PowerShell required; Python preferred)
 Skilled in using performance diagnostics tools (WPA, WPR, Sysinternals, ProcMon, ETW, PerfMon)
 Working knowledge of Active Directory, Group Policy, Azure AD, and hybrid identity models
 Familiarity with DEX tools for endpoint experience monitoring
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Experience with Azure Automation, Power Automate, Logic Apps, Graph API, and automation orchestration platforms
 Experience with application packaging and distribution
 Exposure to endpoint CI/CD pipelines (Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions)
 Understanding of network performance tuning for endpoints
 Knowledge of VDI/AVD environments and Windows 11 performance in virtualized contexts

 Title of Job : Senior Product Acceleration Specialist - Auth0
 Reports to : Director, Product Acceleration
 Job Purpose
 As a Senior Product Acceleration Specialist for Auth0, you will play a critical role in driving customer success, deep product adoption, and long-term retention across Okta’s most strategic Global 2000 (G2K) enterprise accounts. In this highly technical, developer-centric role, you will act as a trusted advisor to enterprise engineering, architecture, security, and application teams, helping them deploy complex, low-friction, high-volume Customer Identity and Access Management (CIAM) solutions on the Auth0 platform. 
 Leveraging your deep Auth0 domain knowledge, you will guide customers through their deployment journeys by supporting key architectural decisions, driving optimal platform usage, and troubleshooting complex technical issues. Operating at the intersection of post-sales support, developer enablement, and product innovation, your core focus will include deploying modern front-end frameworks alongside validating New Product Introductions (NPIs). In doing so, you will act as the essential feedback bridge between G2K engineering teams and Auth0’s Product Management.
 Duties & Responsibilities
 Post-Sales Architectural Advisory & Troubleshooting: Partner directly with G2K Enterprise Customers to guide complex implementation patterns, navigate key architectural decisions, and resolve complex configuration challenges to maximize platform capabilities.
 Pre-Sales & NPI Launch Support: Partner with Sales Engineering and Go-To-Market (GTM) teams during the rollout of New Product Introductions (NPIs). Develop high-impact Proof of Concepts (PoCs), early-adopter demonstrations, and technical enablement assets to help secure technical wins and drive initial pipeline for emerging Auth0 capabilities within G2K accounts.
 Developer Enablement & Prototyping: Assist customer development teams by providing architectural guidance on custom Auth0 Actions, SDK implementation blueprints, and modern full-stack application patterns (Node.js, TypeScript, React, Mobile).
 Product & NPI Feedback Loop: Act as a technical liaison between G2K Enterprise Customers and Auth0 Product Management to identify feature gaps, test early-stage NPIs, and drive product roadmap enhancements based on real-world enterprise needs.
 Field & Customer Mentorship: Create reusable code samples, technical documentation, and enablement guides to train G2K teams (Professional Services, Customer Success, Pre-Sales, Partners) and customer developers on advanced Auth0 capabilities.
 AI Tooling & Automation: Leverage AI tools and LLM workflows to accelerate code generation, SDK debugging, technical documentation, and complex implementation analysis.
 Multi-Project Execution: Manage multiple concurrent technical engagements effectively while prioritizing tasks to ensure high customer satisfaction, which includes providing a rapid, hands-on response to high-priority customer escalations and fast-moving GTM activities.
 Qualifications & Technical Requirements
 Experience: 6+ years in a customer-facing technical field role within a Go-To-Market (GTM) organization (e.g., Pre-Sales/Sales Engineering, Professional Services, Solutions Architecture, Technical Account Management, Customer Success, or Senior Support) delivering identity or SaaS solutions to enterprise accounts.
 Auth0 & CIAM Depth: Expert-level understanding of the Auth0 platform and modern Customer Identity and Access Management (CIAM) patterns, including low-friction authentication, high-volume user management, and extensibility via custom Auth0 Actions.
 Full-Stack Development Skills: Proven experience reading, writing, and debugging full-stack application code using JavaScript/TypeScript, Node.js, React, and modern Mobile SDKs.
 Identity Protocols & Security: Deep understanding of identity federation, access control frameworks, and core protocols including SAML 2.0, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect (OIDC), and SCIM.
 Identity Security & Threat Defense: In-depth knowledge of the CIAM threat landscape, with a proven ability to design and scale resilient authentication flows that mitigate both traditional identity attacks (credential stuffing, account takeover, automated bot attacks, etc.) and emerging next-generation threats (AI-driven social engineering, LLM-based phishing, and automated fraud attacks, etc.)
 G2K Enterprise Experience: Demonstrated history of navigating complex, large-scale IT landscapes, web technologies, and cloud architectures for G2K customers.
 Communication & Advisory: Exceptional ability to translate complex technical/developer concepts to non-technical stakeholders and strategically guide senior engineering leaders.
 Education: A Bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related discipline is required.
